newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end up strong led by mining sector.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end up strong led by mining sector.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed with strong gains Friday, as higher international zinc prices and hopes for solid second quarter company financial results temporarily eclipsed political worries, brokers said.

But they added a recent string of scandals hanging over President Alberto Fujimori still concerned investors. The market's trend next week would largely depend on how well the president uses his July 28 State of the Nation address to help arrest his sudden fall in popularity, they said.
Friday, the General Index rose 3.37 percent to 2,100.9 points, according to preliminary figures.
The blue-chip Selective Index climbed 4.13 percent to 3,012.68 points.

"Zinc has improved today ... There are also some who will take advantage of the low share prices (to buy into) some companies with good long-term prospects," said Manuel Torres from Finvest brokerage.
Fujimori's popularity in the polls has plummeted recently to its lowest level during his seven years in office due to his perceived authoritarianism and allegations of abuses of power.
The crisis has caused jitters on the bolsa, leading to an eight percent overall fall over the last two weeks.
Commentators have predicted Fujimori will use the July 28 independence celebrations' speech to announce measures aimed at stopping his slide in popularity.
Friday's volume was 48 million soles ($18.1 milllion).
Market-leader Telefonica del Peru rose 2.39 percent to 6.42 soles on volume of 750,000 shares.
Miner Morococha recorded the largest increase among leaders, with a 9.42 percent rise to 7.55 soles on a volume of 230,000 shares.
Another polymetal miner Milpo rose 9.97 percent to 43.55 soles on a volume of 42,000 shares.
The country's largest cement producer, Cementos Lima recovered most of Thursday's fall with a 7.5 percent rise to 5.59 soles on a volume of 125,000 shares.
